claims.text: In a cluster randomised trial on 12 medical wards, documented goals-of-care discussions before the last week of life rose from 18 to 41 percent with electronic prompts and training.
claims.passage: documented goals-of-care discussions before the last week of life rose from 18 to 41 percent on intervention wards
claims.interpretation: Prompts plausibly increase documentation enough for a later trial to be worthwhile.

claims.text: After an electronic template was introduced, 63 percent of notes recorded only resuscitation status and 12 percent recorded the patient's values or priorities.
claims.passage: 63 percent of notes contained only resuscitation status and 12 percent documented anything about the patient's values or priorities
claims.interpretation: Documentation counts alone can mislead; note content must be measured.

claims.text: Evidence conflicts on whether a structured template improves the quality of documented conversations: with training and feedback, mean quality rose from 1.8 to 3.9 of 6, while after a template alone it was 2.1 before and 2.3 after.
claims.passage: the mean quality score rose from 1.8 to 3.9 of 6
claims.interpretation: The effect on quality is uncertain and may depend on training and feedback; the quality measure must be shown to work locally before a trial relies on it.

claims.text: After a two-hour calibration, two raters agreed on a six-point quality score for documented conversations with kappa 0.71, taking a median of 6 minutes per note.
claims.passage: After a two-hour calibration session with worked examples, agreement rose to kappa 0.71.
claims.interpretation: Quality rating is feasible but needs calibration and rater time.

claims.text: A postal questionnaire to bereaved next of kin achieved a 34 percent response, lower in deprived neighbourhoods.
claims.passage: The response rate was 34 percent, lower among families of younger patients and in deprived neighbourhoods.
claims.interpretation: Family-reported outcomes need a tested recruitment approach before a trial depends on them.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; one has no stated year. A cluster randomised trial and most studies in a systematic review show that prompts and templates increase documented conversations. The records conflict on quality: a before-after study with training and feedback reported large gains in note quality, while a content analysis after a template alone found notes that mostly recorded resuscitation status and quality scores that barely moved. Only a few studies measured whether care matched patients' goals. A six-point quality score can be rated reliably after calibration, and a family questionnaire reached about a third of bereaved relatives. Documentation is achievable; whether it reflects real conversations is uncertain.
gradeRationale: One randomised trial for documentation, but conflicting uncontrolled evidence on quality, few patient-centred outcomes, and one undated grey report; certainty that the template improves conversations, not only notes, is low.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five claims, one with high uncertainty because the evidence conflicts; overall certainty low.
